subject: United States customary units
hook: UNITED STATES CUSTOMARY UNITS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: United States customary units are not actually based on modern British imperial units, but are instead an older system frozen in time before the British reformed theirs in 1826.
angle_support: The United States customary system of units of 1832 is based on the system in use in the United Kingdom prior to the introduction to the British imperial system on January 1, 1826.
The independence of the U.S. from the British Empire decades prior to the reformation of units in 1824—most notably the gallon... is the cause of the differences in values.
title: Why American Units Are Not British
description: Contrary to popular belief, United States customary units are not simply modern British imperial units. They represent a preserved standard from the colonial era, predating the United Kingdom's significant 1826 standardization of weights and measures.
narration: UNITED STATES CUSTOMARY UNITS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture American measurements as modern British imperial units. It was closer to a time capsule. The U.S. system is a snapshot of Britain before their 1826 reform. When Britain unified their liquid and dry measures into the new imperial gallon, the U.S. had already declared independence. We kept the older Winchester bushel and wine gallon, frozen in place since long before that massive British overhaul. Our units are not modern versions; they are colonial era relics.
